subject: english
question: According to the passage, what is a major reason for limited scope in engineering today?

options.text: Too many graduates and out-dated education

solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 3 (Too many graduates and out-dated education)**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• ***Option 1: Lack of students***

 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The passage highlights oversaturation of graduates, not a shortage of students.
 
 
 
• ***Option 2: No technological growth***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The passage mentions rapid technological changes, not stagnation. The issue is that curricula fail to keep pace with these changes.
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: Too many graduates and out-dated education***
 
 
• This is **correct**. The passage explains that private colleges produce lakhs of engineers every year, leading to oversaturation. At the same time, traditional curriculums fail to provide modern skills, leaving graduates underprepared for industry demands.
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: High salaries for engineers***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The passage does not mention high salaries as a problem; instead, many engineers remain unemployed or accept unrelated jobs.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**: *Too many graduates and out-dated education.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Oversaturation of engineering graduates has created a mismatch between supply and demand in the job market.
 
• Traditional curriculums often fail to adapt to **rapid technological changes**, leaving graduates under-skilled.
 
• Industries now prefer candidates with **practical knowledge and specialised skills** over generic degrees.
 
• Thus, reform in education and focus on **skill-based learning** is essential to restore scope in engineering careers.
